intro: The script fuses two rankings of the same documents with reciprocal rank fusion, then prints how each document's score was built. A document's score is the sum of one small fraction per list it appears in.

c1.title: Two rankings
c1.text: The input: a BM25 list and a vector list over the same documents.

c4.title: Scoring each rank
c4.text: `reciprocal_rank` turns each rank into a small fraction that is added to that document's score.

c5.title: The fused order
c5.text: Sorting by score puts 'C' first, ahead of the BM25 leader.

c6.title: One document explained
c6.text: The breakdown for a document missing from one list.

s3-1cc568.title: BM25 puts A first
s3-1cc568.text: The keyword ranking is the first input; 'A' leads it and 'C' is second.

s53-189112.title: The top rank is worth 0.01639344262295082
s53-189112.text: `reciprocal_rank` gives the top rank 0.01639344262295082, so a first place is worth little more than a second.

s45-ce0cc1.title: Scores after both lists
s45-ce0cc1.text: C ends highest because it is near the top of both lists.

s104-8b1200.title: Sorted by fused score
s104-8b1200.text: The sort puts C at 0.03252247488101534 ahead of A.

s117-f589a6.title: The winner printed
s117-f589a6.text: The report rounds the score to 0.032522.

s156-b082d5.title: A running total starts
s156-b082d5.text: The breakdown adds each list's contribution into `total`.

s222-d2e3b6.title: A document missing from a list
s222-d2e3b6.text: This arm runs only when a document is absent from a ranking, so it adds nothing.

s242-9eb311.title: The total
s242-9eb311.text: The last line prints the summed contribution, 0.016129.
